title: Introduce jurisdictional operator roles and KMS region claim signer
author: Aisha Verma
release_notes: Adds jurisdictional operator role templates, a KMS-backed region-claim signing service, enforcement middleware to reject cross-region operator actions without a signed claim, and audit enrichment with signed provenance headers. Backwards-compatible migration tooling included.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers operating under strict data residency constraints asked for stronger operator-scoping guarantees after a recent support case (SUP-908) revealed ambiguous operator bindings across zones. This PR introduces a formal 'jurisdictional-operator' role family plus a small signer service (kms-claim-signer) that issues KMS-signed region assertions for operator sessions. The goal is to make operator permissions region-aware and cryptographically provable in audit logs and enforcement paths.

Checklist/Scope:
- [x] Add operator role templates and policy mappings for RBAC v2
- [x] Implement kms-claim-signer microservice (signs short-lived region claims using customer or platform CMKs)
- [x] Add enforcement middleware in operator-service and admin-proxy to verify signed claims
- [x] Audit enrichment: include signed-claim headers and signature chain in audit records
- [x] Migration: script to annotate existing operator bindings with recommended jurisdiction tags (best-effort)
- [x] Unit/integration tests + e2e smoke for sample tenant

The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, review notes, and CI behavior.

Commits summary:
- feat(rbac): add jurisdictional-operator role templates and policy compiler hints
- feat(kms-signer): new service that issues signed region-claims; supports both platform CMK and tenant CMK modes
- feat(middleware): enforce signed region claims for operator-scoped endpoints; plumb verification into admin-proxy
- feat(audit): add signature-chain fields to audit proto and forwarder; ensure store compatibility
- chore(migrations): add migration to annotate operator bindings and a reversible db flag
- test: add unit tests for signing/verifying, and add fixture for cross-region rejection

Behavior and compatibility: Enforcement is opt-in per deployment via a new feature flag operator.jurisdictional_enforcement (default off for hosted until rollout). In Dedicated/Private customers we enable by default during onboarding. Requests lacking a signed claim are treated as 'unverified' and are allowed for non-privileged actions; privileged operator actions that require region affinity are rejected with 403.

Migration: A best-effort migration annotates operator bindings using service-zone history and recent request traces; it logs ambiguous mappings to a migration report for ops review.

- rbac/policies/jurisdictional_templates.yaml
- services/kms-claim-signer/{main.go,Dockerfile,README.md}
- services/operator-service/middleware/claim_verifier.go

- infra/helm/operator-jurisdictional-values.yaml
- tests/integration/kms_claim_signer_test.go
- docs/security/jurisdictional-operator.md

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco: requested a threat model and asked for fallbacks when KMS signer is unreachable. Author reply: added retry+cache logic in signer client and a degradation policy that marks claims as 'temporarily-unverifiable' and forces extra MFA for privileged ops.
- Priya: asked whether tenant CMKs could be used and whether signer leaks tenant key material. Author reply: signer only uses Sign API; plaintext keys never leave KMS. Added config to prefer tenant CMK when tenant opts in.
- Liam: flagged possible audit blowup from including full signature blobs. Author reply: switched to compact encoding (signature id + compact sig) and added sampling/retention hints for audit forwarder.

CI summary:
- unit: pass
- integration (kms-signer): pass after two reruns due to transient emulator flakiness
- lint: pass
- e2e smoke: pass
- canary deploy tests (staging): pass

Merge outcome: merged via squash after approvals (Marco approved on 2026-02-23, Priya approved on 2026-02-24).

Post-merge actions:
- Ops run migration in a dry-run mode for two tenant cohorts, then schedule full rollout next week.
- Add monitoring alert for signer error-rate > 1% and migration ambiguity rate > 0.5%

QA notes:
- Verify operator actions to region-bound resources are rejected without signed claim
- Validate audit logs contain signature-chain header and compact signature id
- Test tenant CMK signing path by enabling tenant_kms:true in staging config

Security review: "approved-with-conditions" (conditions: ensure CMK key policies deny Sign to unauthorized principals; rotate signer client's service credentials quarterly).

Risk assessment: Low-to-medium operational risk (new signer is a small service; failure modes are degradable to conservative policies).

Observability: New metrics added: kms_signer_sign_count, kms_signer_error_count, claim_verification_latency_ms, migration_ambiguity_count.
